value: Liver-blood deficiency with internal deficiency heat disturbing the spirit.
Study clues include vexation and insomnia with palpitations, restlessness, dizziness, dry throat or mouth, a red tongue, and a wiry, thin pulse.

value: The direct course-note association is liver-blood deficiency insomnia, summarized by the classical study phrase xu lao xu fan bu de mian.
Use the complete deficiency-heat and liver-blood pattern context rather than insomnia alone when identifying this formula in a study question.

value: Compare with Gui Pi Tang: heart-spleen deficiency emphasizes fatigue, poor appetite, palpitations, and a pale tongue with a thin, weak pulse.
Compare with Huang Lian E Jiao Tang or Liu Wei Di Huang Wan: heart-kidney disharmony emphasizes night sweating, tinnitus, dizziness, and a red tongue with little or no coating.
Compare with Wen Dan Tang: phlegm-heat disturbing the heart emphasizes heaviness of the head, chest fullness, nausea, a greasy yellow coat, and a slippery, rapid pulse.
These are pattern-comparison prompts, not automatic substitutions or treatment recommendations.
